speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm. To help me determine the cause, have you noticed if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your age, bodybuilder status, and the progressive nature of the weakness, have you noticed any muscle wasting, particularly in the forearm or shoulder, or any neck pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: The burning pain you describe alongside weakness and sensory loss is concerning for a neuropathy or nerve compression. Given your history of heavy smoking, anabolic steroid use, diabetes, and significant weight loss, are your symptoms specifically localized to one nerve root, or do they radiate down into your hand? Also, have you noticed any visible muscle wasting in the affected arm?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Diabetes Social history: Drinks 2-7 alcoholic beverages per day. Has smoked 2 packs of cigarettes per day since he was 25. Uses anabolic steroids.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of progressive weakness, sensory loss, burning pain, and significant weight loss in the context of your steroid use and diabetes is highly concerning for a paraneoplastic process or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Given the severity of the symptoms and the potential for a serious underlying malignancy, I need to visualize the cervical spine and brain immediately. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI and Brain_MRI. Also, please confirm if you have noticed any difficulty with your handwriting or buttoning your shirt, which would indicate hand muscle weakness.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent fevers, changes in vision, difficulty speaking, or changes in balance.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Paraneoplastic Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS) secondary to underlying malignancy (likely Lung Cancer given smoking history).
